newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan plans to raise telecom cap for foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan plans to raise telecom cap for foreigners.

text.p: Taiwan is planning to revise its telecommunications law to let foreign investors own stakes of up to one third in Taiwan's telecom services, up from 20 percent at present, local newspapers said on Friday.
The agreement was reached by relevant government agencies as part of the island's latest bid to join the World Trade Organisation, the Commercial Times newspaper said.

The Economic Daily News said Taiwan, under intense pressure to open its telecom market, is also considering allowing a more flexible interpretation of foreign interests that in effect can raise the foreign ownership cap to up to 50 percent.
Friday was a public holiday and officials could not be reached for comment.
The revision needs approval from cabinet and parliament.

Under reform laws enacted in January 1996, foreign interests may own 20 percent of Taiwan firms offering common-carrier services, a ratio designed by parliament to ensure local control of what is considered a strategic resource.
Common-carrier services are the main telephone and data lines in Taiwan's telecom network, including mobile telephony and retail telephone services.
Since January 1996, foreigners have been allowed to own and operate internet services, airline reservation systems and other value-added services that piggy-back common carrier networks.
In January 1997, Taiwan awarded eight lucrative mobile phone franchises to local consortiums, most of them paired with global telecom giants as minority partners.
